description.short_caption: Axial CT of the abdomen showing intra-abdominal findings.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial CT image of the abdomen. The scan shows multiple abdominal structures, including the liver, stomach, intestines, and retroperitoneal space. There is evidence of abnormal fluid collections in the peritoneal cavity, suggestive of ascites. The bowel loops appear mildly distended, and there is a possible thickening of the intestinal wall, which could indicate inflammation or infection. The image is in grayscale, with contrast-enhanced structures visible.
visible_findings: abnormal fluid collections in the peritoneal cavity

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung fields with areas of abnormality. There are patchy, ground-glass opacities visible in both lungs, particularly in the periphery. The mediastinum appears central, and no significant pleural effusion is noted. The image is de-identified and shows no patient-identifying information.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thoracic cavity. There are bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, more prominent in the lower lung zones, with areas of increased opacity. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size, and the diaphragm is well-defined. No obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact.
visible_findings: increased opacity in lower lung zones

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the pelvis showing soft tissue and bony structures.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the pelvis demonstrates the bony structures, including the iliac bones and sacrum, as well as soft tissue structures. There is a central density in the pelvic cavity, which may represent a foreign body, calcification, or other pathology. The image is de-identified and includes clear labeling of right (R) and left (L) sides.
visible_findings: bony structures of the pelvis visible
soft tissue structures in the pelvic cavity
central density in the pelvic cavity

description.short_caption: Acid-fast stain showing red-stained organisms against a pale background.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an acid-fast stain with multiple red-stained, round to slightly irregular structures against a pale background. The red staining indicates the presence of acid-fast organisms, likely mycobacteria. The background appears granular and lightly stained, consistent with cellular debris or extracellular material. The image is magnified to highlight the organisms' morphology.

Case_09012/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Growth of liver aspirate on MacConkey agar.

description.short_caption: Growth of liver aspirate on MacConkey agar showing pink, lactose-fermenting colonies.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a MacConkey agar plate with bacterial growth. The colonies appear pink, indicating lactose fermentation. The plate is being held in a gloved hand, and the background includes laboratory equipment. The growth pattern suggests the presence of a Gram-negative, lactose-fermenting organism, commonly associated with enteric bacteria.
visible_findings: growth pattern consistent with Gram-negative bacteria

description.short_caption: String test demonstrating viscous colonies on an agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with multiple white, mucoid colonies on a red agar medium. A blue loop tool is being used to lift one of the colonies, demonstrating a string-like, viscous consistency characteristic of certain bacterial species, such as Klebsiella pneumoniae. The background is blurred, focusing attention on the colonies and the string test being performed.
visible_findings: blue loop tool lifting a colony

description.detailed_description: This image shows a MacConkey agar plate with multiple large, mucoid colonies. The colonies appear hypermucoviscous, with a shiny and sticky appearance, consistent with certain bacterial strains known for this phenotype. The agar has a reddish hue typical of MacConkey agar, which is used to differentiate lactose-fermenting from non-lactose-fermenting organisms. Some areas of the plate are obscured by black redaction marks.
visible_findings: black redaction marks obscuring parts of the plate
